grid.origin: row 0 = north edge, same grid as client/habitat.png

encoding.index: species_mix_index.png: the cell's row in mixes (0 = no mix: the client's habitat-class mix). 8-bit grey; with index_bytes 2, RGB with the row = R + 256 G
encoding.density: species_mix_density.png RGB: R tree_density, G shrub_density, multiplier = byte / 100 on the client's per-habitat-class plant count (1.0 = the fixed-mix count; the count still scales with client/canopy.png cover); B unused. The same bytes as the row's density_bytes
encoding.weights: mixes[].tree_bytes and shrub_bytes: [[species id, byte], ...], the species with a non-zero weight in the column order of `species`, each layer summing to 255 (absent: no trees or no shrubs). The client draws a species by walking this list in order, so the order is part of the format
encoding.terrain: mixes[].terrain: the terrain classes (effective elevation band, floor / mid-slope / steep, north) whose cells use the row; a community (communities[], one per source and code: its name, the weights and densities as written, and a note) has one row per distinct terrain response (pipeline species_mix.py TERRAIN), and mixes[].community names it. The bytes are after the terrain factors
